adjudications.rationale: The revision closes the prior segment-scope defect: segment is required in the elected decision, bound in the credential, verified against actual local context, and fails closed on absence/mismatch. The fallback if no exact-match scope caveat exists is explicitly named as needing a new key, not silently assumed.

The induction now has a non-poisonable base case: unanimous signed genesis, self-signature rejection, non-circular run_id, replay nonce, fixed epoch N thresholds, and genesis binding on all transitions. It also rejects liveness-derived shrinkage and distinguishes genesis unanimity from runtime majority.

The ruling still blocks the hunt-item attack: mode (a) is only a positively elected downgrade while quorum exists, with expiry failing closed to mode (b). Quorum loss cannot trigger weak mode or keep it open indefinitely, especially when read with M-23's conjunctive clock/epoch/segment bounds.

The amended caveat preserves the key boundary: BFT claims apply only to verified elected decisions, not unilateral local-store writes. It coherently classifies mode (a) as a downgrade and names the mint-path verification premise with the correct consequence if false.
